questions.question: This does not compile. Which change keeps `retryCount` a non-null `Int` that is assigned later, and does compile?
questions.explanation: `lateinit` is not allowed on primitive types like `Int`, because it uses `null` in the field to mean "not assigned yet" and an unboxed `int` field can't hold `null`. `Delegates.notNull()` works for any type and throws `IllegalStateException` if you read it before assigning. `lateinit` also rejects nullable types, `val` and initializers.

questions.question: What does this print?
questions.explanation: Property initializers run top to bottom. When `doubled` is initialized, `base` hasn't been assigned yet, so the function reads the default `0` and the result is `0`. The compiler only catches a direct reference, not one that goes through a function.

questions.question: A `lateinit var` can be assigned again after it has been initialized.
questions.explanation: `lateinit` only postpones the first assignment. The property is still a `var`, so you can reassign it as many times as you like (for example, a new adapter after a config change).

questions.question: What does this print?
questions.explanation: The `lazy` initializer runs only on the first access, and the result is cached. The second read returns the same `v1` without running the block again, so `calls` stays `1`.

questions.question: Which of these `lateinit` declarations compile? Select all that apply.
options: `lateinit var token: String` at the top level of a file
`lateinit var tags: List<Int>` in a class
`lateinit var msg: String` as a local variable in a function
`lateinit val id: String` in a class
`lateinit var user: User?` in a class
questions.explanation: `lateinit` works on top-level, member and local `var`s of non-null, non-primitive types. It is rejected on `val`, on nullable types, and on properties with a custom getter or setter.

questions.question: A Fragment uses this pattern. A network callback that finishes after the user navigates away (the fragment goes to the back stack) calls `binding.title.text = ...`. What happens?
options: The text is updated on the old, detached view and nothing else happens
The update is queued and applied when the view is recreated
questions.explanation: After `onDestroyView` sets `_binding` to null, the `binding` getter's `!!` throws an NPE. The pattern frees the view hierarchy while the fragment sits on the back stack, but callbacks must be scoped to `viewLifecycleOwner` so they stop when the view is destroyed. It is a nullable property, not `lateinit`, so the exception is not `UninitializedPropertyAccessException`.

questions.question: What does this print?
questions.explanation: `::title.isInitialized` reports whether the `lateinit` backing field has been assigned yet, without throwing. It is `false` before the assignment and `true` after.

questions.question: A Fragment declares `private val binding by lazy { FragmentFeedBinding.inflate(layoutInflater) }` and returns `binding.root` from `onCreateView`. What is the bug?
options: The lazy never resets, so old views leak on the back stack and are reused when the view is recreated
`lazy` cannot be used in a Fragment, so it fails to compile
The binding is inflated again on every access, so views are duplicated each time `binding` is read
`layoutInflater` is always null inside a `lazy` block, so the first access crashes with `NullPointerException`
questions.explanation: A `lazy` `val` is computed once and can't be reset, but a Fragment's view can be destroyed and recreated many times. The cached binding keeps the old views alive after `onDestroyView` and hands stale views back to the next `onCreateView`. Use the nullable `_binding` pattern that is cleared in `onDestroyView`.

questions.explanation: If the initializer throws, `lazy` stores nothing, so the next access runs the block again. The second access succeeds and caches `ok after 2`, which the third access reuses. The failure is not cached as a permanent exception.

questions.question: What happens with this code?
options: Compile error: `base` must be initialized before `doubled` reads it
questions.explanation: The compiler sees a direct read of `base` before it is initialized and reports "variable 'base' must be initialized". Hiding the same read behind a function call compiles and silently reads `0`.

questions.question: If code reads a `lateinit` member property before it is assigned, the compiler reports an error.
questions.explanation: The compiler can't track when a member property gets assigned, since that might happen in a lifecycle callback or by DI. The check happens at runtime: reading it too early throws `UninitializedPropertyAccessException`.

questions.question: `by lazy` is meant to defer work safely, yet the parent constructor touches it first. What does this print?
questions.explanation: `by lazy` stores a hidden delegate field (`name$delegate`) that is assigned in `Child`'s initializer, which runs after `Base`'s `init`. When `Base` calls the overridden `describe()`, that delegate field is still null, so reading `name` throws a NullPointerException instead of running the lambda. Once construction finishes, the lazy works normally. Lazy does not protect you from calling open members in a constructor.

questions.question: An Activity declares `private val viewModel: FeedViewModel by viewModels()` and, right below it, `private val title = viewModel.title`. What happens when the Activity starts?
options: It crashes with `IllegalStateException`: the ViewModel is requested before the Activity has an Application
It works, because `by viewModels()` creates the ViewModel eagerly when the property is declared
It works, because property initializers run after `onCreate`
It compiles to a `lateinit` field and throws `UninitializedPropertyAccessException` when `title` is first read
questions.explanation: `by viewModels()` is a lazy delegate, but `title`'s initializer reads it during construction. That happens before `onCreate`, when the Activity has no Application yet, so the ViewModel lookup throws. Read the ViewModel in `onCreate` or later, or make `title` lazy too.

questions.question: Which statements about the default `by lazy { ... }` are true? Select all that apply.
options: It can only back a `val`, not a `var`
Its default mode is synchronized, so the initializer runs once even if several threads race to read it
You can reset it by assigning `null`, which makes the next read recompute it
Its initializer runs when the enclosing object is constructed
questions.explanation: `Lazy` only has `getValue`, so using it on a `var` is a compile error. Its default mode is `SYNCHRONIZED`. There is no way to reset it, and the initializer runs on first access, not at construction.

questions.question: `MainActivity.onCreate` runs `ImageCache.context = this`. What is the problem?
options: The singleton holds the Activity, so destroyed Activities leak; use `applicationContext` instead
`lateinit` cannot hold a `Context`, so it doesn't compile
The `lazy` block runs again on every rotation, so the cache dir is recreated and old files are lost
Nothing, because `object` properties are cleared automatically when the Activity that set them is destroyed
questions.explanation: An `object` lives as long as the process, so a stored Activity can't be garbage-collected after it is destroyed. Its views and resources leak with it. `dir` is computed only once either way, and the cache dir is app-wide, so storing `context.applicationContext` gives the same result without the leak.

questions.question: What does this print?
questions.explanation: Reading an unassigned `lateinit` throws `UninitializedPropertyAccessException`. `Delegates.notNull()` is an ordinary delegate that throws `IllegalStateException` ("Property age should be initialized before get."). Neither one throws an NPE.

questions.question: After a default `by lazy` value has been computed, the `Lazy` object still holds the initializer lambda and everything it captured.
questions.explanation: The stdlib implementation sets its `initializer` reference to null once the value is stored, so whatever the lambda captured can be garbage-collected. Before the first access, though, the lambda and its captures are held. That still includes `this`, such as an Activity.

questions.question: `title` is a public `lateinit` property. Why does this fail to compile?
options: `isInitialized` needs access to the backing field, which only the declaring class (or same file) has
`isInitialized` only works on `private` lateinit properties, and `title` is public
Bound references like `s::title` are not allowed on `var` properties
`isInitialized` needs `kotlin-reflect` on the classpath, which Android projects don't include by default
questions.explanation: `isInitialized` inspects the backing field, so K2 reports "backing field ... is not accessible at this point" from outside `Screen`, even though `title` is public. Expose a helper such as `fun hasTitle() = ::title.isInitialized` inside the class.

questions.question: In an Activity, `adapter` is created in `onCreate` with a click listener and replaced when the user switches tabs. Which declaration fits best?
questions.explanation: The value is assigned from outside, in a lifecycle callback, and is reassigned later. That calls for `lateinit var`. `lazy` suits a `val` that can compute itself once and never change, and `lateinit val` doesn't compile.
